channel.title: Weekly Digest
channel.description: The week's main stories from your sources

item.title: Tech leaders push for AI slowdown as U.S. and China clash over regulation
item.description: Major AI companies are advocating for a slower development pace, while Trump labels opposition to AI as a conspiracy. The U.S. and China are in conflict over AI regulation amid global concerns about its impact on human rights. Why it matters: The debate over AI regulation reflects broader geopolitical and ethical tensions with significant implications for technology development and human rights. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Al Jazeera, Ara, BBC World, El País, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, Público, RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump's mail-in voting restrictions
item.description: The US Supreme Court rejected Trump's attempt to limit mail-in voting ahead of midterms, citing insufficient time for state implementation. The decision preserves current voting rules but does not resolve the legality of Trump's policies. Outlets note the ruling could impact election access for millions. Why it matters: The ruling may affect voting access for millions and could influence the outcome of upcoming midterm elections. (Sources: Al Jazeera, El País, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Sánchez targets end-of-year resolution for Ceuta crisis
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has set a goal to stabilize the situation in Ceuta by the end of the year, addressing migration and diplomatic tensions. He dismissed claims of Moroccan blackmail using Pegasus spyware as fake news, while his opacity on the matter has fueled suspicions among allies. Why it matters: The situation in Ceuta has significant implications for Spain's migration policy and international relations. (Sources: 20minutos, El País, Nació Digital, Público, RTVE, eldiario.es)

item.title: Electoral Board Divided on Supreme Court's Vote Suspension Order
item.description: Spain's Central Electoral Board split 7-6 to comply with a Supreme Court ruling suspending voting rights for naturalized citizens under the Grandchildren's Law. The decision includes measures to verify exiled status and adjust census data at consulates. Why it matters: The ruling affects over 400,000 citizens' voting rights and highlights tensions between judicial and political branches. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Ara, El País, La Directa, La Vanguardia, Público, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Leaders from Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland unite for self-determination
item.description: Leaders from Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland have signed a declaration supporting self-determination. They argue that Westminster has no right to block democratic processes and demand constitutional reform. The leaders called for an end to the current political relationship with the UK. Why it matters: This agreement could reshape the political landscape of the UK and its relationship with its constituent nations. (Sources: 3Cat (324), Ara, El País, Nació Digital, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Israeli NGO accuses government of pursuing 'elimination' project in West Bank
item.description: An Israeli NGO claims Israeli authorities are using violence, mobility restrictions, and economic pressure to undermine Palestinian life in the West Bank. Multiple sources report that these actions are part of a coordinated effort to erode Palestinian collective existence. Some outlets note that the strategy has intensified since the formation of Netanyahu's government in 2022. Why it matters: The alleged 'elimination project' could have long-term consequences for Palestinian society and its ability to sustain itself in the occupied territories. (Sources: Al Jazeera, El País, La Vanguardia, RTVE, eldiario.es)
